marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: Name the following: (i) The drainage pattern seen in 9185.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Radial
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) 9185 – Radial
key_points: Drainage pattern in 9185 is Radial
marking_schemes.model_answer: Radial
common_errors: Some candidates wrote 'flows in all direction from the centre' instead of using the technical term 'radial pattern'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the four drainage patterns — Dendritic, Trellis, Radial and Disappearing — with the help of diagrams. Lay stress on the use of technical terms.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: Name the following: (ii) The pattern of settlement seen in 9787.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Scattered / Dispersed
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) 9787 – Scattered / Dispersed
key_points: Settlement pattern in 9787 is Scattered or Dispersed
marking_schemes.model_answer: Scattered / Dispersed
common_errors: Some candidates wrote 'huts are far from each other' instead of using the technical term 'scattered settlement'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay stress on the use of technical terms.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: What do the following symbols mean? (i) 3r in 9089.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) 3r in 9089 – the relative height of the earthwork embankment is 3 meters.
key_points: 3r in 9089 indicates the relative height of the earthwork/embankment is 3 meters
marking_schemes.model_answer: 3r in 9089 indicates the relative height of the earthwork embankment is 3 meters.
common_errors: Several candidates explained the conventional symbols instead of giving the technical term — Relative Height of embankment
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Revise conventional symbols and landform features regularly with students.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: What do the following symbols mean? (ii) 200 in 9383.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) 200 in 9383 – the value of the contour line is 200 m above mean sea level.
key_points: 200 in 9383 indicates the value of the contour line is 200 metres above mean sea level
marking_schemes.model_answer: 200 in 9383 indicates that the value of the contour line is 200 metres above mean sea level.
common_errors: Majority of candidates were unable to differentiate between contour, contour height or contour line
Many wrote contour interval
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the contour structure of all land forms present in the syllabus with the help of cross-section.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: Name two types of vegetation found in the region east of easting 93.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Dense mixed jungle, open scrub.
key_points: Dense mixed jungle
Open scrub
marking_schemes.model_answer: The two types of vegetation found in the region east of easting 93 are dense mixed jungle and open scrub.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote evergreen forest, deciduous forest or tropical monsoon forest instead of dense mixed jungle and open scrub
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students to answer questions on maps from what they observe on the maps and not from their theoretical knowledge.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: Give two evidences which suggest that the rainfall received in the region shown on the map extract is seasonal.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Seasonal streams / seasonal tanks / dry tank / broken ground. (Any two) Seasonal river with water channel / dry stream.
key_points: Seasonal streams
Seasonal tanks / dry tank
Broken ground
Seasonal river with water channel / dry stream
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two evidences of seasonal rainfall visible on the map are the presence of seasonal streams (or dry streams) and seasonal/dry tanks or broken ground.
common_errors: Most candidates wrote evidences of seasonal rainfall other than those observed on the given map — they used theoretical knowledge instead of map observation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students to answer questions on maps from what they observe on the maps and not from their theoretical knowledge.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: Calculate the area of the region between 85 – 90 northing and 90 – 95 easting. Give your answer in kilometer.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: There are 25 grid squares in this boundary limit. Scale of map is 2 cm = 1 km. Area of 1 grid square is 1 km² ∴ Area of 25 squares is 25 km².
key_points: There are 25 grid squares in the specified boundary
Scale of map is 2 cm = 1 km
Area of 1 grid square is 1 km²
Total area = 25 km²
marking_schemes.model_answer: The region between 85–90 northing and 90–95 easting contains 25 grid squares. Since the scale is 2 cm = 1 km, each grid square has an area of 1 km², giving a total area of 25 km².
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise the significance of writing the unit for any value — area, distance, length, breadth or height.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: Mention any two manmade features and two natural features in grid square 9080.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Manmade features – cart track / cultivated land / permanent hut / Temple / Ranawas settlement / lined perennial well. (Any two) Natural features – seasonal stream / plain / broken ground / disappearing stream / barren land / dry river / intermittent stream. (Any two)
key_points: Manmade: cart track
Manmade: cultivated land
Manmade: permanent hut
Manmade: Temple
Manmade: Ranawas settlement
Manmade: lined perennial well
Natural: seasonal stream
Natural: plain
Natural: broken ground
Natural: disappearing stream
Natural: barren land
Natural: dry river / intermittent stream
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two manmade features in grid square 9080 are cart track and cultivated land (or permanent hut/Temple/Ranawas settlement/lined perennial well). Two natural features are seasonal stream and plain (or broken ground/disappearing stream/barren land/dry river/intermittent stream).
common_errors: Most candidates could write manmade features but were unable to mention natural features
Some candidates wrote tree as a natural feature, which is incorrect as trees may grow naturally or may be planted
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide and help students to learn the difference between man-made and natural features on the map. Also explain broken ground and broken land.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: What is the direct distance in kilometers between the surveyed tree west of Rampura (9580) to the Chhatri in Juvol (9282)?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 6.7 cm. Scale is 2 cm = 1 km. ∴ 6.7 cm = 6.7 ÷ 2 = 3.35 km ~ (3–4 km). (accepted range 3.25 – 3.45 km) i.e. 6.5 – 6.9 cm
key_points: Measured distance on map is approximately 6.7 cm
Scale is 2 cm = 1 km
Direct distance = 3.35 km (accepted range 3.25 – 3.45 km)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The measured distance on the map between the surveyed tree west of Rampura and the Chhatri in Juvol is approximately 6.7 cm. Using the scale of 2 cm = 1 km, the direct distance is approximately 3.35 km (accepted range: 3.25 – 3.45 km).
common_errors: Many candidates did not write the unit (km)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise the significance of writing the unit for any value. Demonstrate the use of twine to measure the distance.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: Mention: (i) The most commonly used means of transport in the area shown on the map extract.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Cart track / Pack track
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Cart track / pack track
key_points: The most commonly used means of transport is cart track or pack track
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cart track / Pack track
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: Mention: (ii) The main occupation of the people of the region in the southeastern part of the map extract.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Cultivation / Agriculture / Farming
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Cultivation / Agriculture / Farming.

marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: (i) What is the compass direction of Rampura (9580) from Karja (9781)?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: South West
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) South west

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map sheet No. 45D/7 and answer the following questions: (ii) Identify the landform marked by contours in 9782.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Conical hill / Valley / Spur / Water shed / Escarpment / Steep slope
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Conical hill / valley / spur / water shed / escarpment / steep slope.
key_points: Landform in 9782 is a conical hill, valley, spur, watershed, escarpment, or steep slope

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (a) Shade and label Thar desert.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – Thar desert correctly shaded and labelled in northwestern Rajasthan.
key_points: Thar desert shaded in correct location (northwestern Rajasthan)
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade the Thar desert in northwestern Rajasthan and label it correctly.
common_errors: Majority demarcated a very large area extending into Punjab, Haryana, UP and Gujarat
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the exact location of deserts and give adequate practice in shading as per the asked question.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (b) Label the river Narmada.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – River Narmada correctly marked and labelled.
key_points: River Narmada marked in correct location
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark and label the river Narmada flowing westward through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise the use of arrows for marking rivers and making sure that the arrow head points towards the feature. The rivers can be outlined in blue and their names written on top of the line.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (c) Shade and name the Wular lake.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – Wular Lake correctly shaded and named in Jammu & Kashmir.
key_points: Wular Lake shaded in correct location (north of river Jhelum, J&K)
Correctly named
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade and name the Wular Lake located north of the river Jhelum touching its northern bend in Jammu & Kashmir.
common_errors: Some candidates marked the Wular Lake over a very large area
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Tell the students that the Wular Lake is located north of the river Jhelum touching its northern bend.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (d) Shade and label Kanara coast.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – Kanara coast correctly shaded and labelled.
key_points: Kanara coast shaded in correct location
Correctly labelled without extending into Malabar/Konkan coast
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade and label the Kanara coast correctly within its defined extent on the western coast of India.
common_errors: Most candidates shaded the Kanara coast beyond its extent into Malabar/Konkan coast
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students about the extent of the coast.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (e) Mark and name Mount Kanchenjunga.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – Mount Kanchenjunga correctly marked and named on the India-Nepal-Sikkim border.
key_points: Mount Kanchenjunga marked at correct location on India-Nepal-Sikkim border
Correctly named
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark and name Mount Kanchenjunga at the correct location on the Sikkim-Nepal border.
common_errors: A number of candidates marked Nathula as Mount Kanchenjunga
A few candidates marked it in Nepal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice to students in marking the correct location of hills/mountain peaks on maps.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (f) Shade and label a densely-populated region in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – A densely populated region correctly shaded and labelled (e.g. Ganga plain, West Bengal).
key_points: A valid densely populated region shaded within India's boundaries
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade and label a densely populated region such as the Ganga Plain or West Bengal within India's boundaries.
common_errors: Some shaded the Ganga plain extending into Nepal
A few shaded entire West Bengal extending into Bangladesh
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to shade regions within India's boundaries only.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (g) Shade and label a region with Red soil in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – Region with red soil correctly shaded and labelled.
key_points: Red soil region correctly identified and shaded
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade and label a region with red soil such as parts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, or Odisha.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the topic on minerals and soils thoroughly along with adequate practice on the map.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (h) Mark with a dot and name Chennai.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – Chennai correctly marked with a dot and named on the southeastern coast.
key_points: Chennai marked with a small dot at correct location on southeastern coast
Correctly named
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark Chennai with a small dot on the southeastern coast of India (Tamil Nadu) and name it.
common_errors: In some cases, Chennai was marked with a big dot which extended into the water body
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to mark cities with small dots. Instruct students not to extend ports or cities into the water body.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (i) Mark and label the Arabian Sea branch of S.W. Monsoon.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – Arabian Sea branch of S.W. Monsoon correctly marked with arrow and labelled.
key_points: Arabian Sea branch of S.W. Monsoon marked with arrow in correct direction
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark the Arabian Sea branch of the S.W. Monsoon with an arrow pointing towards the western coast of India and label it correctly.
common_errors: In few cases, the arrow head was marked incorrectly/horizontally
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: While teaching the topic on climate, lay stress that the angle/direction of the arrow/arrow head must be marked correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: (j) Mark with a dot and name Singhbhum.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: MAP – Singhbhum correctly marked with a dot and named in Jharkhand.
key_points: Singhbhum marked with a dot in correct location in Jharkhand
Correctly named
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark Singhbhum with a dot in Jharkhand and name it correctly.
common_errors: Most candidates marked Singhbhum in Orissa instead of Jharkhand
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the topic on minerals thoroughly along with adequate practice on the map.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is the winter rainfall of the northwest part of India different from the winter rainfall of the southeast part of India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rainfall in northwest part of India occurs due to temperate cyclone whereas in south east part of India it is due to winter monsoon / retreating monsoon.
key_points: Northwest India winter rainfall is caused by temperate cyclones (Western Disturbances)
Southeast India winter rainfall is caused by winter monsoon / retreating monsoon
marking_schemes.model_answer: Winter rainfall in northwest India is caused by temperate cyclones (Western Disturbances), whereas winter rainfall in southeast India is caused by the retreating/winter monsoon winds picking up moisture from the Bay of Bengal.
common_errors: Some candidates gave a long explanation without breaking it into distinct points
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to write the differences in a tabular form, point wise and with the basis for distinction. Discourage students from writing answers in long drawn explanations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name a state that is the first to experience the onset of the monsoon.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Kerala
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Kerala
key_points: Kerala is the first state to experience the onset of the monsoon
marking_schemes.model_answer: Kerala
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned the place (city) instead of the state
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to read the question carefully to avoid careless mistakes.

marking_schemes.question_text: How does the 'Mango shower' influence the state of Karnataka?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Mango shower helps in early ripening of Mango crop and is also helpful for tea / coffee cultivation in Karnataka.
key_points: Mango shower helps in early ripening of the Mango crop
It is also helpful for tea/coffee cultivation in Karnataka
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Mango shower helps in the early ripening of the mango crop and is also beneficial for tea and coffee cultivation in Karnataka.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: (i) Kanyakumari experiences equable climate.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Kanyakumari is near the sea and is also near the equator and so has equable climate.
key_points: Kanyakumari is near the sea (maritime influence)
Kanyakumari is near the equator
marking_schemes.model_answer: Kanyakumari experiences equable climate because it is located near the sea and is also close to the equator, both of which moderate its temperature.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Through classroom discussions, give adequate practice to answer reasoning questions which require thorough knowledge and conceptual clarity.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: (ii) Central Maharashtra gets less rainfall than the coastal area of Maharashtra.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Central Maharashtra lies in the rain shadow area whereas coastal Maharashtra is on the windward side of Western Ghats.
key_points: Central Maharashtra lies in the rain shadow area of the Western Ghats
Coastal Maharashtra is on the windward side of the Western Ghats
marking_schemes.model_answer: Central Maharashtra lies in the rain shadow area of the Western Ghats and therefore receives less rainfall, whereas coastal Maharashtra is on the windward side and receives heavy rainfall.
common_errors: Several candidates wrote vague reasons without mentioning rain shadow area or windward side
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Through classroom discussions, give adequate practice to answer reasoning questions which require thorough knowledge and conceptual clarity.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for each of the following: (iii) Jaipur has a higher annual range of temperature than Mumbai.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) Jaipur lies in continental interior whereas Mumbai lies close to the sea. Thus, Jaipur has extremes of temperature, but Mumbai has equable climate.
key_points: Jaipur lies in the continental interior and has extreme temperatures
Mumbai lies close to the sea and has equable climate
marking_schemes.model_answer: Jaipur lies in the continental interior and experiences extremes of temperature (high annual range), whereas Mumbai is located close to the sea and experiences equable climate with a lower annual range of temperature.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to write answers to the point, emphasising on key words.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write three differences between summer monsoon season and retreating monsoon season.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Summer Monsoon Season: Wind is onshore from S.W. direction. Heavy rain, high humidity, high temperature. There is rain in almost whole country. Retreating Monsoon Season: Wind direction is north east / withdrawal of monsoon. Clear sky, high temperature, low humidity. There is no rain in most parts of India but when wind picks up moisture from Bay of Bengal it brings rain to coromandel coast.
key_points: Summer Monsoon: winds blow onshore from S.W. direction; Retreating Monsoon: wind direction is N.E. / withdrawal of monsoon
Summer Monsoon: heavy rain, high humidity, high temperature; Retreating Monsoon: clear sky, high temperature, low humidity
Summer Monsoon: rain in almost the whole country; Retreating Monsoon: no rain in most parts except Coromandel coast (rain due to NE winds picking moisture from Bay of Bengal)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Summer Monsoon blows onshore from the S.W. and brings heavy rain, high humidity, and high temperature to almost the whole country. Retreating Monsoon involves northeastward withdrawal of winds, resulting in clear skies and low humidity over most of India, with rain confined to the Coromandel coast as the northeast winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote differences between summer season and rainy season instead of summer monsoon season and retreating monsoon season
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to write the differences in a tabular form, point wise and with the basis for distinction.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why does alluvial soil differ in texture?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It varies in texture as it is deposited by rivers. Coarse material is deposited in higher altitude areas and fine material is brought to lower plain / transported soil.
key_points: Alluvial soil is a transported/river-deposited soil
Coarse material is deposited at higher altitudes; fine material is deposited in lower plains
marking_schemes.model_answer: Alluvial soil differs in texture because it is transported and deposited by rivers — coarse material settles at higher altitudes while fine material is carried further and deposited in the lower plains.
common_errors: Majority got confused between Khadar and Bhangar
Some did not mention the key point that alluvial soil is a transported soil
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that students have clarity of concepts. Lay stress on the correct use of terminology.

marking_schemes.question_text: State two cash crops that grow well in alluvial soil.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Sugarcane / Jute / Cotton / Tobacco / Oilseed (any two)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Sugarcane / Jute / Cotton / Tobacco / oilseed
key_points: Any two of: Sugarcane, Jute, Cotton, Tobacco, Oilseed
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sugarcane / Jute / Cotton / Tobacco / Oilseed (any two)
common_errors: Many candidates wrote food crops instead of cash crops
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide the students to write precise answers with the key words.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to black soil answer the following: (i) Name one important crop which grows in this soil.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Cotton / Sugarcane / Tobacco / Cereals / Oil seeds / Jowar / Wheat / Gram (any one)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Important crop grown in black soil is cotton / sugarcane / tobacco / cereals / oil seeds / jowar / wheat / gram.
key_points: Any one of: Cotton, Sugarcane, Tobacco, Cereals, Oil seeds, Jowar, Wheat, Gram
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cotton / Sugarcane / Tobacco / Cereals / Oil seeds / Jowar / Wheat / Gram (any one)

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to black soil answer the following: (ii) Give one chemical property of this soil.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Chemical property – Rich in lime, potash, calcium & magnesium carbonate. Poor in phosphorous nitrogen and organic matter LIMCAP / non-acidic / non-alkaline.
key_points: Rich in lime, potash, calcium and magnesium carbonate (LIMCAP)
Poor in phosphorous, nitrogen and organic matter
Non-acidic / non-alkaline
marking_schemes.model_answer: Black soil is rich in lime, potash, calcium and magnesium carbonate (LIMCAP) but poor in phosphorous, nitrogen and organic matter. It is non-acidic and non-alkaline in nature.
accepted_alternatives: rich in calcium and magnesium carbonate
common_errors: Most candidates wrote physical properties of black soil instead of chemical properties
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the conservation methods in detail. Ensure that students have clarity of concepts.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one geographical reason for each of the following: (i) Red soil requires irrigation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Red soil need irrigation as it does not retain moisture since it is highly porous.
key_points: Red soil is highly porous and does not retain moisture, hence requires irrigation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Red soil requires irrigation because it is highly porous and does not retain moisture well.
common_errors: Most candidates stressed on dry farming; very few mentioned porous soil and low moisture retention
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the students that red colour of the soil is due to ferric oxide or iron oxide (rust), not due to iron. Ensure that students have clarity of concepts.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one geographical reason for each of the following: (ii) Afforestation prevents soil from getting eroded.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) The roots of the trees hold the soil together.
key_points: Tree roots hold the soil together, preventing erosion
marking_schemes.model_answer: Afforestation prevents soil erosion because the roots of the trees bind the soil particles together, holding them in place.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the conservation methods in detail.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one geographical reason for each of the following: (iii) Laterite soil is red in colour.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) Rich in iron oxide
key_points: Laterite soil is red due to its richness in iron oxide (ferric oxide)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Laterite soil is red in colour because it is rich in iron oxide (ferric oxide/rust).
common_errors: Some candidates wrote 'presence of iron' instead of 'iron oxide' or 'ferric oxide'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the students that red colour of the soil is due to ferric oxide or iron oxide (rust), not due to iron.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is soil erosion?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Removal and destruction of soil is called soil erosion.
key_points: Soil erosion is the removal and destruction of the top layer of soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Soil erosion is the removal and destruction of the top layer of soil by natural agents such as wind and water.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote that soil erosion is degradation through pollution instead of removal of top soil by agents of aggradation and degradation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise to the students that complete definitions have to be written.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two causes of soil erosion in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Causes – deforestation / poor farming techniques / overgrazing / wind / heavy rainfall / human activities / running water / shifting cultivation.
key_points: Deforestation
Poor farming techniques
Overgrazing
Wind
Heavy rainfall
Human activities
Running water
Shifting cultivation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two causes of soil erosion in India are deforestation and overgrazing (or poor farming techniques, heavy rainfall, shifting cultivation, running water, wind).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain the differences between the causes and agents of soil erosion.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name an area in India where Tropical Monsoon forest is found.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) It is found in Northern states along foot hills of Himalayas, Eastern slopes of Western Ghats, Siwalik range and Chota Nagpur plateau region.
key_points: Northern states along foothills of Himalayas
Eastern slopes of Western Ghats
Siwalik range
Chota Nagpur plateau region
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical Monsoon forests are found in northern states along the foothills of the Himalayas, on the eastern slopes of the Western Ghats, in the Siwalik range, and in the Chota Nagpur plateau region.
common_errors: Most candidates wrote the name of the state or about geographical conditions instead of naming a specific area
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to read and understand the question carefully.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is Tropical Monsoon forest of great commercial value to India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) This forest has commercially valuable trees i.e. teak, sal, and shisham which yield valuable timber. It is easily accessible / pure stand.
key_points: Contains commercially valuable trees — teak, sal, and shisham which yield valuable timber
Easily accessible / pure stand
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical Monsoon forests are of great commercial value as they contain commercially valuable timber trees such as teak, sal, and shisham. These forests are also easily accessible and form pure stands.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Do a constant revision of the topics taught.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to Littoral forest, answer the following questions: (i) Why do the trees in this forest grow aerial roots?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Aerial root helps the trees to survive in marshes, creeks and submerged areas.
key_points: Aerial roots help trees survive in marshes, creeks and submerged areas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Trees in Littoral forests grow aerial roots to help them survive in waterlogged, marshy, and submerged areas such as creeks and deltas.
common_errors: Many candidates were unable to answer correctly as they considered 'Littoral' as the name of a tree rather than a type of vegetation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students the characteristic features of Littoral vegetation, different trees, uses of the trees and regions where this vegetation is found.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to Littoral forest, answer the following questions: (ii) Name one area in India where this forest is found.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Along deltas of large rivers of east coast / Sunderban / coastal areas of West Bengal / Andhra Pradesh / Orissa / Andaman Nicobar / deltaic area of Godavari / Mahanadi / Krishna (any one area)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Along deltas of large rivers of east coast, Sunderban, coastal areas of West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, Andaman Nicobar / deltaic area of Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna.
key_points: Any one area: Sunderban, coastal West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh coast, Orissa coast, Andaman & Nicobar, deltaic areas of Godavari/Mahanadi/Krishna
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sunderban / coastal areas of West Bengal / Andhra Pradesh / Orissa / Andaman & Nicobar / deltaic areas of Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna (any one)
common_errors: A few candidates named a state instead of naming an area
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students the regions where Littoral vegetation is found.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name a state in India where thorn and scrub forest is found.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: S.W. Punjab / U.P. / Central & eastern Rajasthan / M.P. / Gujarat (any one)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) S.W. Punjab, U.P., Central & eastern Rajasthan, M.P., Gujarat.
key_points: Any one of: S.W. Punjab, U.P., Central & eastern Rajasthan, M.P., Gujarat
marking_schemes.model_answer: S.W. Punjab / U.P. / Central & eastern Rajasthan / M.P. / Gujarat (any one)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay emphasis on reasoning questions. Do a constant revision of the topics taught.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two ways by which the trees found in thorn and scrub forest have adapted to the climate.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Trees have adapted by developing long roots, leaves turning to spines, thick fleshy stems to store water, drought resistant / xerophytic.
key_points: Developing long roots to reach deeper water sources
Leaves modified into spines to reduce water loss
Thick fleshy stems to store water
Drought resistant / xerophytic adaptations
marking_schemes.model_answer: Trees in thorn and scrub forests have adapted to the dry climate by developing long roots to access deep water sources and by modifying their leaves into spines to reduce water loss. They also develop thick, fleshy stems to store water and are generally drought-resistant (xerophytic).

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two ways in which forests are important.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Forests are moderators of climate, play important role in carbon cycle, control soil erosion, help water percolation, add humus to soil and are habitat for animals and birds. Maintain ecological balance.
key_points: Forests moderate climate / play role in carbon cycle
Control soil erosion
Help water percolation
Add humus to soil
Habitat for animals and birds
Maintain ecological balance
marking_schemes.model_answer: Forests are important because they moderate climate and play a vital role in the carbon cycle, controlling soil erosion and helping water percolation. They also add humus to the soil, serve as habitats for wildlife, and help maintain ecological balance.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay emphasis on reasoning questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one forest conservation method followed in India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Afforestation / Re-afforestation / Van Mahotsav / Social forestry / Farm forestry / Agroforestry / Silviculture / Joint forest management (any one)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Afforestation / re-afforestation / Van Mahotsav / social forestry / farm forestry, agroforestry / silviculture / joint forest management.
key_points: Any one of: Afforestation, Re-afforestation, Van Mahotsav, Social forestry, Farm forestry, Agroforestry, Silviculture, Joint forest management
marking_schemes.model_answer: Afforestation / Re-afforestation / Van Mahotsav / Social forestry / Farm forestry / Agroforestry / Silviculture / Joint forest management (any one)

marking_schemes.question_text: There is plenty of rain in India during the rainy season, yet we need irrigation. Give two reasons to support this statement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rain is erratic and seasonal / annual crops like sugarcane need plenty of water throughout growing period / crops like rice need plenty of water / lot of loss of water due to evaporation on account of tropical climate / HYV seeds.
key_points: Rain is erratic and seasonal
Annual crops like sugarcane need water throughout growing period
Crops like rice need plenty of water
Lot of loss of water due to evaporation in tropical climate
HYV seeds require assured irrigation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Despite heavy rainfall during the rainy season, irrigation is needed because rainfall in India is erratic and seasonal, leaving crops without water in dry months. Additionally, water-intensive crops like sugarcane and rice need a continuous water supply throughout their growing period, and significant water is lost to evaporation in the tropical climate.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify with examples the difference between modern methods and traditional methods of irrigation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name three traditional means of irrigation.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Wells, canals, tanks
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Traditional means – wells, canals, tanks.
key_points: Wells
Canals
Tanks
marking_schemes.model_answer: Wells, canals, tanks
common_errors: Some were confused about tube wells (tube wells are a modern method)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify with examples the difference between modern methods and traditional methods of irrigation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason why traditional means of irrigation are still important in most parts of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Traditional means have low initial cost burden / easy to operate / easily accessible to farmers.
key_points: Low initial cost burden
Easy to operate
Easily accessible to farmers
marking_schemes.model_answer: Traditional means of irrigation are still important because they have low initial cost, are easy to operate, and are easily accessible to small farmers in most parts of India.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Do a comparative study by making a flow chart of different methods of irrigation along with their advantages and disadvantages.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Surface water and Ground water.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Surface Water – Water available in lakes, ponds, river and streams / polluted. Ground water – water available below land in aquifer / pure / improve quality of ground water.
key_points: Surface water: water available in lakes, ponds, rivers and streams; often polluted
Ground water: water available below the land surface in aquifers; generally purer
marking_schemes.model_answer: Surface water is the water available in lakes, ponds, rivers and streams and is often polluted. Ground water is the water stored below the land surface in aquifers and is generally purer in quality.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two reasons to explain as to why we are facing water scarcity in recent times.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) We face water scarcity as a lot of water is either wasted or polluted. Demand of pure potable water is therefore, more than its supply.
key_points: A lot of water is wasted or polluted
Demand for pure potable water exceeds supply
marking_schemes.model_answer: We face water scarcity because a large amount of water is either wasted or polluted. As a result, the demand for pure, potable water far exceeds its supply.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is rain water harvesting?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) It is the procedure of augmenting the natural filtration of rain water to recharge groundwater and storing it in underground reservoirs, borewells, dug wells etc.
key_points: Rain water harvesting is the procedure of augmenting natural filtration of rainwater to recharge groundwater and storing it in underground reservoirs, borewells, dug wells etc.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rain water harvesting is the procedure of augmenting the natural filtration of rainwater to recharge groundwater and store it in underground reservoirs, borewells, dug wells, etc.

marking_schemes.question_text: What are the advantages of rain water harvesting?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) To increase the ground water table, to meet the demands of increased population and agricultural activities.
key_points: Increases the ground water table
Meets demands of increased population and agricultural activities
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rain water harvesting helps increase the ground water table and meets the growing demands of an increasing population and expanding agricultural activities.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name two water harvesting systems practised in India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Rain water Harvesting / Roof top harvesting system / Ground water recharge (any two)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) 1. Rain water Harvesting 2. Roof top harvesting system 3. Ground water recharge. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Rain water Harvesting, Roof top harvesting system, Ground water recharge
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rain water Harvesting and Roof top harvesting system (or Ground water recharge)

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two advantages that non-conventional energy sources have over conventional energy sources.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Advantage – They produce large amount of power, which can be used for domestic, industrial and other activities. / renewable / eco-friendly / inexhaustible
key_points: Renewable / inexhaustible sources of energy
Eco-friendly (do not cause pollution)
Produce large amounts of power usable for domestic and industrial activities
marking_schemes.model_answer: Non-conventional energy sources are renewable and inexhaustible, unlike conventional sources. They are also eco-friendly and produce large amounts of power for domestic and industrial use.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to make maps and tables to facilitate learning.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one advantage of the use of natural gas over coal or petroleum.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Natural gas creates less pollution (if used as CNG or LPG) as compared to fossil fuels such as coal or petroleum.
key_points: Natural gas (CNG/LPG) creates less pollution compared to coal or petroleum
marking_schemes.model_answer: Natural gas, when used as CNG or LPG, creates significantly less pollution compared to fossil fuels such as coal or petroleum.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students the difference between off shore and on shore oil fields with examples and locations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name one off shore oil field of India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Mumbai High / Aliabet / Bassein / basin of Godavari / Krishna / Cauvery (any one)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Mumbai High / Aliabet / Bassein / basin of Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery.
key_points: Any one of: Mumbai High, Aliabet, Bassein, Godavari basin, Krishna basin, Cauvery basin
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mumbai High / Aliabet / Bassein / basin of Godavari / Krishna / Cauvery (any one)
common_errors: Some candidates named Digboi as an off-shore oil field (Digboi is an on-shore oil field)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students the difference between off shore and on shore oil fields with examples and locations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Answer the following: (i) State one industrial use of copper.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Copper is used for making wire and for alloys
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Copper is used for making wire and for alloys.
key_points: Copper is used for making electrical wire
Copper is used for making alloys
marking_schemes.model_answer: Copper is used industrially for making electrical wires and for manufacturing alloys.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay emphasis on reasoning questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Answer the following: (ii) Mention one advantage of generating power from bio-gas.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Non-polluting / waste put to good use / residue used as manure / inexhaustible / reduces dependence on fossil fuels / cleans environment.
key_points: Non-polluting
Waste is put to good use
Residue used as manure
Inexhaustible
Reduces dependence on fossil fuels
Cleans environment
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of generating power from bio-gas is that it is non-polluting, the waste is put to good use, and the residue can be used as manure.

marking_schemes.question_text: Answer the following: (iii) Name the mineral that toughens steel and makes it rust-proof.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Manganese
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) Manganese is used to make steel tough and rust proof.
key_points: Manganese toughens steel and makes it rust-proof
marking_schemes.model_answer: Manganese
common_errors: Some candidates wrote magnesium, iron, and aluminium instead of manganese

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the metal obtained from Bauxite. Give any one use of the metal mentioned by you.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Aluminium; used to make utensils, aircrafts, in automobiles, wires
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Aluminium – it is used to make utensils, aircrafts, in automobiles, wires.
key_points: Metal obtained from Bauxite is Aluminium
Uses: making utensils, aircrafts, automobiles, wires
marking_schemes.model_answer: The metal obtained from Bauxite is Aluminium. It is used to make utensils, aircraft, automobiles, and wires.

marking_schemes.question_text: Which multi-purpose project provides power to both Punjab and Himachal Pradesh?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Bhakra Nangal
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Bhakra Nangal.
key_points: Bhakra Nangal multi-purpose project provides power to both Punjab and Himachal Pradesh
marking_schemes.model_answer: Bhakra Nangal

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the cultivation of tea answer the following: (i) Why is tea grown on hill slopes?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Tea cannot bear stagnant water and so sloping ground is suitable.
key_points: Tea cannot bear stagnant water; sloping ground ensures proper drainage
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tea is grown on hill slopes because it cannot bear stagnant water. Sloping ground ensures proper drainage of excess water.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote reasons related to aroma, flavour and taste, which are incorrect geographical reasons
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that the students learn the correct range of temperature and the rainfall requirement of crops.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the cultivation of tea answer the following: (ii) Why tea bushes have to be pruned at regular intervals?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Pruning encourages the production of fresh leaves and shoots / To keep it at a low height to facilitate plucking.
key_points: Pruning encourages production of fresh leaves and shoots
Keeps the bush at low height to facilitate plucking
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tea bushes are pruned at regular intervals to encourage the production of fresh leaves and young shoots, and to keep them at a manageable height for easy plucking.
common_errors: A few candidates confused between the terms pruning and ratooning
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the concept of pruning along with its benefits.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to rice cultivation answer the following: (i) Why does the cultivation of rice require a lot of manual labour?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Rice has to be transplanted in puddled fields for better crop / it has to be harvested carefully by sickle – all this require lot of labour.
key_points: Rice has to be transplanted in puddled fields for better crop
It has to be harvested carefully by sickle
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rice cultivation requires a lot of manual labour because it has to be transplanted in puddled fields for better crop yield and harvested carefully by hand using a sickle — both operations that cannot be easily mechanised.
common_errors: The answers given by the majority of candidates reflected lack of understanding of the topic
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to write complete and precise answers.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to rice cultivation answer the following: (ii) Mention two geographical conditions which suit the cultivation of rice.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Temperature – 20°C - 32°C / 16°C - 32°C. Rain – 150 – 300 cm. Soil – alluvial with a subsoil of clay. (Any two)
key_points: Temperature: 20°C–32°C (or 16°C–32°C)
Rainfall: 150–300 cm
Soil: alluvial with a subsoil of clay
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rice cultivation requires a temperature of 20°C–32°C and an annual rainfall of 150–300 cm. It grows best in alluvial soil with a subsoil of clay (any two).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that the students learn the correct range of temperature and the rainfall requirement of crops.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for each of the following: (i) Cotton is a labour-intensive crop.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Cotton is propagated by sowing seeds on the farm / Cotton has to be protected against weevils and other insects, therefore, pesticides have to be sprayed / Cotton is a soil exhausting crop, therefore, fertilizers have to be used / Mechanized harvesting of cotton is not possible, has to be done manually which goes on for three months. (Any one)
key_points: Cotton is propagated by manual seed sowing
Must be protected against pests — pesticides have to be sprayed manually
Cotton is soil-exhausting — fertilizers must be applied
Mechanized harvesting is not possible; manual harvesting goes on for three months
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cotton is a labour-intensive crop because mechanised harvesting is not possible and picking has to be done manually over a period of three months. It also requires manual spraying of pesticides to protect against weevils and application of fertilisers as it is a soil-exhausting crop. (Any one reason accepted.)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give ample practice in reasoning-type questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for each of the following: (ii) Jute is retted after it has been harvested.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Submerging the harvested jute stalks in clean running water facilitates the removal of the fibre from the bark / softening by microbiological process.
key_points: Submerging jute stalks in clean running water facilitates removal of fibre from the bark
The softening occurs through a microbiological process
marking_schemes.model_answer: Jute is retted (submerged in clean running water) after harvesting because the water facilitates the removal of the fibre from the bark through a microbiological softening process.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay stress on the important geographical terms so that students can retain them and write the correct terminology.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for each of the following: (iii) The growing of pulses is important in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) Pulses are a source of proteins, particularly for the vegetarians / good as a rotation crop / leguminous, therefore has nitrogen fixing quality in the soil / used as cattle feed. (Any one)
key_points: Pulses are a source of protein, especially for vegetarians
Good as a rotation crop
Leguminous — nitrogen-fixing quality improves soil fertility
Used as cattle feed
marking_schemes.model_answer: Growing pulses is important in India because they are a rich source of protein for the largely vegetarian population, serve as a good rotation crop, and being leguminous, fix nitrogen in the soil, thus improving soil fertility. (Any one reason accepted.)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain that growing of pulses is important as it is a source of protein, a leguminous crop that replenishes soil fertility and fixes nitrogen.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is agriculture important in India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) It is important as it provides employment, raw material for industries and export surplus / provides food and fodder.
key_points: Provides employment
Provides raw material for industries
Contributes to export surplus
Provides food and fodder
marking_schemes.model_answer: Agriculture is important in India because it provides employment to a large section of the population, supplies raw material to industries, contributes to export surplus, and provides food and fodder.
common_errors: Several candidates could not write the specific points highlighting the importance of agriculture
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to write complete and precise answers.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the two main agricultural seasons of India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Rabi and Kharif
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Rabi / Kharif
key_points: Rabi
Kharif
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rabi and Kharif
common_errors: Many candidates wrote 'summer crop' and 'winter crop season' instead of Rabi and Kharif
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay stress on the important geographical terms so that students can retain them.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is mixed farming?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) It is growing of crops along with an allied occupation such as dairy farming, bee keeping etc.
key_points: Mixed farming is the growing of crops along with an allied occupation such as dairy farming, bee keeping, etc.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mixed farming is the practice of growing crops along with an allied occupation such as dairy farming, bee keeping, poultry, etc.
common_errors: Mixed farming was not explained correctly by many candidates

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the private sector iron and steel plant of India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) / Tata Steel
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Tata iron and steel company (TISCO) / Tata Steel
key_points: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) / Tata Steel is the private sector iron and steel plant
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) / Tata Steel
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that students learn the areas/mines from where the minerals are obtained.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the private sector iron and steel plant of India (TISCO/Tata Steel). From where does it get its supply of: 1. Iron ore, 2. Manganese, 3. Coal?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: 1. Iron ore: Gurumahsani in Mayurganj, Naomundi in Singhbhum. 2. Manganese: Joda in Keonjhar / Naomundi. 3. Coal: Jharia / Bokaro
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1. Gurumahsani in Mayurganj, Naomundi in Singhbum. 2. Joda in Keonjhar / Naomundi. 3. Jharia / Bokaro
key_points: Iron ore: Gurumahsani in Mayurganj, Naomundi in Singhbhum
Manganese: Joda in Keonjhar / Naomundi
Coal: Jharia / Bokaro
marking_schemes.model_answer: TISCO gets iron ore from Gurumahsani in Mayurganj and Naomundi in Singhbhum; manganese from Joda in Keonjhar or Naomundi; and coal from Jharia or Bokaro.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the names of the states instead of the mining centres
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that students learn the areas/mines from where the minerals are obtained.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention any two problems faced by the cotton textile industry of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Agro-based industry, therefore the fluctuation in the supply of raw material / low productivity of labour / obsolete machinery and outdated methods of production / sick industrial units / shortage of power / competition from other countries like Egypt / competition from synthetic fibre. (Any two)
key_points: Fluctuation in supply of raw material (agro-based)
Low productivity of labour
Obsolete machinery and outdated production methods
Sick industrial units
Shortage of power
Competition from countries like Egypt
Competition from synthetic fibre
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two problems faced by the cotton textile industry of India are: fluctuation in supply of raw material due to its agro-based nature, and competition from synthetic fibre as well as from other countries like Egypt. (Any two from the list accepted.)

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for each of the following: (i) Silk industry is doing particularly well in Karnataka.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Favourable climate for rearing silkworms (bombyx mori) / Soft water free from alkaline salt is available / Traditional occupation therefore plenty of skilled labour. (Any two)
key_points: Favourable climate for rearing silkworms (bombyx mori)
Soft water free from alkaline salt is available
Traditional occupation with plenty of skilled labour
marking_schemes.model_answer: Silk industry is doing particularly well in Karnataka because the state has a favourable climate for rearing silkworms (Bombyx mori), soft water free from alkaline salts is available, and it is a traditional occupation with a large pool of skilled labour. (Any two reasons accepted.)

skilled labour due to traditional occupation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain with examples the meaning of petrochemical products.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for each of the following: (ii) Petrochemical products are gaining popularity in modern times.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Petrochemicals are cost effective, durable, cheaper, and available in plenty / generation of employment / not dependent on agriculture.

Generation of employment
Not dependent on agriculture
marking_schemes.model_answer: Petrochemical products are gaining popularity because they are cost effective, durable, cheaper than natural alternatives, available in plenty, generate employment, and are not dependent on agriculture for raw materials.

marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain with examples the meaning of petrochemical products, the reasons for popularity of petrochemicals products and the reason for concentration of petrochemical industry.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for each of the following: (iii) The electronics industry is proving to be an asset for our country in the field of education.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name a city most famous for electronics and hence called 'The Electronics Capital of India'.

marking_schemes.model_answer: Rourkela, located in the Sundergarh district of Odisha at the confluence of the Sankha and Koel rivers, is the iron and steel industry set up with German collaboration.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name a by-product of sugar industry which is used in the manufacture of wax and shoe polish.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Press mud
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) Press mud.
key_points: Press mud is a by-product of the sugar industry used in making wax and shoe polish
marking_schemes.model_answer: Press mud
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach at least three by-products of sugar industry along with their uses.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two reasons for the 'means of transport' being called the lifelines of a nation's economy.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Means of transport help the economy by helping in movement of goods & raw material for industrial growth / export & import / infrastructure development / growth of tertiary sector.
key_points: Facilitate movement of goods and raw material for industrial growth
Enable export and import
Contribute to infrastructure development
Support growth of the tertiary sector
marking_schemes.model_answer: Means of transport are called the lifelines of a nation's economy because they facilitate the movement of goods and raw materials essential for industrial growth and enable exports and imports. They also support infrastructure development and the growth of the tertiary sector.
accepted_alternatives: movement of goods and raw material
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach both positive and negative aspects of the different modes of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two ways in which rail transport is useful for the people of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Railways: Easy movement of bulky goods. / It has brought the villages close to cities. / Helps during natural calamities. / Journey is comfortable. / Provides employment.
key_points: Easy movement of bulky goods
Brought villages closer to cities
Helps during natural calamities
Journey is comfortable
Provides employment
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rail transport is useful for the people of India because it enables easy movement of bulky goods and has brought villages closer to cities. It also provides comfortable journeys, helps during natural calamities, and provides large-scale employment.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Conduct quizzes and group discussions for active participation of students.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one advantage of inland waterways.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) It is cheaper, eco-friendly / low maintenance.
key_points: Inland waterways are cheaper and eco-friendly / require low maintenance
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of inland waterways is that they are cheaper, eco-friendly, and require low maintenance.
common_errors: Many candidates confused inland waterways with overseas transport
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain to students the difference between inland waterways and sea routes.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one advantage of roadways.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Cheaper / door to door service / safer movement of goods / links other means of transport.
key_points: Cheaper
Provides door-to-door service
Safer movement of goods
Links other means of transport
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of roadways is that they provide door-to-door service and are cheaper. They also link other means of transport and enable safer movement of goods. (Any one accepted.)

marking_schemes.question_text: State one disadvantage of water transport.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) It is time consuming / depends on weather / can cause sea sickness.
key_points: Time consuming
Depends on weather conditions
Can cause sea sickness
marking_schemes.model_answer: One disadvantage of water transport is that it is time consuming, depends on weather conditions, and can cause sea sickness. (Any one accepted.)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach both positive and negative aspects of the different modes of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give three reasons as to why airways are becoming a popular means of transport in modern India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Airways are faster. Comfortable. Can cross natural barriers with ease. Provide quick help in natural calamities.
key_points: Airways are faster
Comfortable mode of travel
Can cross natural barriers with ease
Provide quick help in natural calamities
marking_schemes.model_answer: Airways are becoming a popular means of transport in modern India because they are faster and more comfortable than other modes. They can cross natural barriers such as mountains and rivers with ease and also provide quick assistance during natural calamities.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay emphasis on reasoning questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two reasons as to why there is a need for safe waste disposal.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: - waste accumulation causes pollution of air, soil & water and so it needs to be managed properly. - It leads to spread of diseases. - foul smell. - spoils scenic beauty.
key_points: Waste accumulation causes pollution of air, soil and water
It leads to the spread of diseases
Causes foul smell
Spoils scenic beauty
marking_schemes.model_answer: Safe waste disposal is needed because waste accumulation causes pollution of air, soil and water, which harms health and the environment. It also leads to the spread of diseases, causes foul smell, and spoils the scenic beauty of an area.
accepted_alternatives: pollution of air, soil and water
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain clearly about wastes, their types and methods of their safe disposal.

marking_schemes.question_text: How can waste be reused? Explain with the help of an example.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Waste can be reused by giving the discarded material another shape or form i.e. waste paper can be reused by making paper bags, discarded bottles can be used for storage purpose.
key_points: Waste can be reused by giving discarded material another shape or form
Example: waste paper can be made into paper bags; discarded bottles can be used for storage
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste can be reused by giving discarded material another shape or form. For example, waste paper can be made into paper bags, or discarded bottles can be reused for storage purposes.
common_errors: Majority of candidates were unable to explain how waste could be reused; some gave examples without explaining the concept
A few gave incorrect examples
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss concepts of reduce, reuse and recycling of wastes through examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one way in which waste accumulation has an effect on the following: (i) aquatic life
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Aquatic life: fish & other aquatic animals may die due to pollution created by waste.
key_points: Fish and other aquatic animals may die due to pollution created by waste accumulation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste accumulation pollutes water bodies, which can cause fish and other aquatic animals to die.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote about oil spills instead of general waste pollution
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instruct students to read and understand the question carefully before answering.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one way in which waste accumulation has an effect on the following: (ii) terrestrial life
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Terrestrial life: Waste looks ugly, leads to foul smell, attract insects, rodents etc. pollute air, water, harms plant kingdom.
key_points: Waste attracts insects and rodents
Pollutes air and water
Harms the plant kingdom
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste accumulation affects terrestrial life by attracting insects and rodents, polluting air and water, and harming the plant kingdom.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one way in which waste accumulation has an effect on the following: (iii) landscape
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) Landscape: It makes the landscape look ugly.
key_points: Waste accumulation makes the landscape look ugly
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste accumulation makes the landscape look ugly and degrades its visual appeal.

marking_schemes.question_text: What do you mean by the following terms? (i) Segregation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (i) Segregation – It means dividing the waste separately by sorting degradable from non-degradable substances.
key_points: Segregation means dividing waste by sorting degradable from non-degradable substances
marking_schemes.model_answer: Segregation refers to the process of dividing waste by sorting degradable substances from non-degradable ones.
common_errors: Majority of candidates could not write the specific points highlighting the meaning of segregation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to learn the important geographical terms and associated activities related to them.

marking_schemes.question_text: What do you mean by the following terms? (ii) Composting.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ii) Composting – It is an aerobic method of decomposing of organic waste.
key_points: Composting is an aerobic method of decomposing organic waste
marking_schemes.model_answer: Composting is an aerobic method of decomposing organic waste to produce nutrient-rich compost.

marking_schemes.question_text: What do you mean by the following terms? (iii) Dumping.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (iii) Dumping – In this method waste is dumped in open low-lying area far from the city.
key_points: Dumping is the method in which waste is deposited in open low-lying areas far from the city
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dumping is a method of waste disposal in which waste is deposited in open low-lying areas located far from the city.
